thread:
maria_cs: Heads-up: Acme (canary) seeing a burst of 429s right after deploys. Pattern: 15-45s window of preflight 429s during SDK init, then stabilizes. They only hit it when traffic goes through their edge (CloudFront w/ HTTP/3 enabled).
eli_support: Can you paste a sample request_id and the SDK version? Also whether this is browser or server SDK?
maria_cs: request_id=rid_e9c4f1; sdk=0.11.0; env=server-node; region=eu-west-1; sample log: `2026-03-22T08:07:12Z rid_e9c4f1 INIT start; 2026-03-22T08:07:13Z rid_e9c4f1 PRECHECK 429; retry-after: 1s; conn_proto: h3; via: cloudfront`
acme-sre: We spin up a fleet of lambdas with coldstart parallelism ~20. Each lambda does SDK init on start. Our ephemeral token TTL is ~10s but due to some clock skew we often see ~6s remaining when init runs.
sam_sre: Quick hypothesis: parallel init + short token TTL -> stampede and preflight gating trips. Plus some HTTP/3 proxies re-order or strip client-id headers causing per-ip/conn rate keys to collide.
jen_devx: Agreed. Also worth checking whether the edge terminates and re-establishes QUIC connections upstream causing our per-connection heuristics to error. If many upstream connections are created quickly, our token preflight counters may exceed soft limits.
eli_support: Two low-friction tests: 1) flip the SDK to staggered init (concurrency=3, jitter 0-300ms) via env vars: `REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_MAX_PARALLEL=3` and `REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_JITTER_MS=300`; 2) temporarily disable HTTP/3 at CloudFront so traffic falls back to HTTP/2 and see if the spike disappears. Can the SRE try both and report numbers?
acme-sre: Running test now. Also we have token refresh code that does `if (expires_in <= 5) refresh()` which will refresh aggressively. We'll add a randomized 100-500ms delay when multiple processes detect low ttl.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary/acme sdk-config patch applied (env set: REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_MAX_PARALLEL=3, REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_JITTER_MS=300) at 2026-03-22T08:09:40Z
acme-sre: First pass: after applying staggered init we see preflight 429s drop ~78% in the first 30s. With HTTP/3 still enabled we get a smaller tail of 429s at scale. Disabling HTTP/3 entirely drops bursts to near zero.
jen_devx: That strongly implicates protocol/edge behavior + concurrency stampede. Recommend we ship a short onboarding note that calls out: "If using HTTP/3/QUIC edge proxies, prefer staggered SDK init or disable H3 for preflight-heavy workloads." Also add an SDK change to make staggered init the default for server environments where concurrency >4.
eli_support: Action items: (1) Maria: send customer the quick-config snippet + a short troubleshooting checklist; (2) Jen: add onboarding blurb and short runbook for preflight 429s with edges; (3) Sam: keep monitoring canary p90/rate for 24h and post a summary; (4) Alex (runtime): open ticket to revise rate-keying to prefer idempotent header keys and tolerate truncated Via/XFF.
maria_cs: I'll send the snippet and propose a 25-minute follow-up call with Acme tomorrow at 09:00 UTC to confirm renewal is safe.
acme-sre: Thanks — we'll keep HTTP/3 off for the next 24h while we validate. If we need to re-enable later we'll stage a gradual roll.
jen_devx: I'll draft the onboarding note and a short paragraph for the renewal enablement pack (so CSMs can reference it during calls).
eli_support: Please file the runtime ticket and paste the id back here so we can coordinate CS and engineering prioritization.
sam_sre: Monitoring will keep sampling 30s windows and will escalate if preflight rate > 50/min for canary.
alex_backend: (later) opened RUN-4839 with hypothesis + logs + suggested fix for header-based keying.
acme-sre: Confirmed: concurrency=3 + jitter + HTTP/3 off = clean starts in our stage cluster. We'll validate in prod tomorrow morning.
